subject: Post-call: multilingual suitability sprint — model shortlist & validation plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Larsson <emma.larsson@nordicpay.com>, Kenji Saito <kenji.saito@tokutech.jp>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: multilingual suitability sprint — model shortlist & validation plan

Hi Emma & Kenji,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the multilingual suitability sprint we discussed:

Summary of needs (from call)
- NordicPay: prioritizing Swedish + Danish conversational support for payments flows (NPS-sensitive).
- TokuTech: pilot Japanese + English auto-responses for support tickets (strict token budget per turn).
- Shared ask: low latency (~150–200ms token tail), deterministic safety filters, and clear regression tracking for locale-specific failure modes.

Initial model shortlist (recommended by Redwood based on call signals)
- Llama-3-70B-instruct (int8) — strong multilingual reasoning, recommended for Swedish/Scandinavian QA and long-form prompts.
- Mistral-7B-turbo (4-bit quant) — efficient option for high-throughput Japanese/English classification and short responses.
- Redstone-13B-quant-lite — (internal/redwood-verified) candidate for constrained-cost paths; we suggest evaluating for parity vs Llama-3 on Swedish fallback cases.

Proposed validation plan (what we'll run in the sprint)
1) Dataset & prompt freeze (we'll ask you to confirm 200 representative examples per locale)
2) Benchmarks: BLEU/ChrF for NLG, acceptance-rate for intents, and a small set of human evals (3 raters, two-tier rubric focusing on accuracy + cultural appropriateness).
3) Regression watchlist: synonyms, date/number formatting, honorific handling (JP), ambiguous currency mentions.
4) Latency/cost profile: full token-level trace for 1k calls per model to estimate unit costs.

Deliverables & timeline
- Day 0: prompt set + sample data (you) — please share by 2027-09-05.
- Day 3–5: Redwood runs automated bench + quick smoke tests; share benchmark CSV and initial failure triage.
- Day 6–10: Human eval tranche + short readout call.

Attachments: initial prompt pack + suggested rubric (multilingual-prompt-pack-v1.zip), preliminary benchmark template (benchmark-summary-metrics.csv).

Immediate asks for Emma/Kenji
1) Confirm target locales and one business-critical flow per locale (reply inline).
2) Confirm date for prompt/data drop (we suggested 2027-09-05).
3) Any compliant data restrictions (PII redaction rules) we should enforce up-front?

If that all looks OK I’ll assign Neha as the evaluation lead and Ben as the ops contact for throughput profiling.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

---
Attachment: multilingual-prompt-pack-v1.zip (archive, 24 files: per-locale prompt templates + rubrics)
Attachment: benchmark-summary-metrics.csv (CSV template)
From: Emma Larsson <emma.larsson@nordicpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kenji Saito <kenji.saito@tokutech.jp>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: multilingual suitability sprint — model shortlist & validation plan

Thanks Karthik — really clear, appreciate the plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed locales: Swedish (sv-SE) primary, Danish (da-DK) secondary. We want bot-handled payment flow + an escalation path for merchant disputes.
- Data: we can share 250 anonymized transcripts for Swedish and 150 for Danish. All PII will be redacted but note we do have obfuscated PAN tokens we must preserve for fraud signals. Does Redwood need the PAN tokens masked or replaced?
- For human evals: we prefer raters who understand Nordic idioms; can Redwood supply raters with regional language experience, or should we bring a vendor?

Also — curious about the Redstone variant: is that a Redwood-managed model or external? Any public perf numbers vs Llama-3 for low-frequency Swedish lexical items?

I'll aim to get the sample drop by 2027-09-05 but if we need to push to 2027-09-07 we can.

Best,
Emma Larsson
Head of Product Localization | NordicPay
emma.larsson@nordicpay.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Larsson <emma.larsson@nordicpay.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: multilingual suitability sprint — model shortlist & validation plan

Hi Emma — quick answers inline below.

> Does Redwood need the PAN tokens masked or replaced?
Please keep PAN obfuscated (e.g., <PAN_REDACTED>) rather than completely removing the token sequence. We instrument special-casing in the prompt templates so the model sees the placeholder context for fraud-signal heuristics without exposing raw PII.

> For human evals: can Redwood supply raters with regional language experience?
Yes — we have vetted raters for Swedish/Danish through our ops partners; we can run the human evals with Redwood-managed raters or accept your vendor if you prefer. There is a small fee for Redwood-managed regional evaluations (T&Cs in the Drive link).

> Redstone variant: managed by Redwood; it is our lightweight-quant path that trades depth for cost. We have internal benchmarks for Swedish lexical coverage — in our tests Redstone matched Llama-3 on intent classification (±2%) but fell behind on rare-lemma NLG cases (~6–8% lower adequacy). We recommend including it as a cost-control arm of the sprint but not the primary NLG candidate.

If you need a two-day slip to 09-07 that’s fine — we’ll shift the automated bench window accordingly. Confirm which date and I’ll lock resources.

Thanks — assigning Neha to coordinate the prompt set ingestion.

Karthik
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Larsson <emma.larsson@nordicpay.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 09:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: multilingual suitability sprint — model shortlist & validation plan

Emma — thanks for confirming. Two operational notes and an action list from the eval team: 

Operational notes
- Data ingestion: please upload the anonymized transcripts to the shared Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBqExampleMultilingualSprint (use the locale-prefixed CSV names). I will run a quick schema check and report back within 24 hours.
- Raters: Redwood-managed Swedish/Danish raters are available; cost estimate attached in the MAP-qualitative-notes.pdf. If you opt to use your vendor, we need them on-boarding details by 2027-09-08.

Action items (owners & deadlines)
- Emma: upload locale CSVs (swedish_transcripts.csv, danish_transcripts.csv) — due 2027-09-07 (owner: Emma).
- Karthik: finalize model config matrix (quant levels, batching targets) — due 2027-09-03 (owner: Karthik).
- Neha: run automated bench and provide benchmark-summary-metrics.csv — due 2027-09-10 (owner: Neha).
- Ben: run throughput/latency profiling across Llama-3 & Mistral candidates (1k calls sample) — due 2027-09-08 (owner: Ben).

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: Swedish rare-lemma generation may regress under 4-bit quantization.
  Mitigation: include Llama-3 int8 as the high-accuracy arm; add prompt engineering and targeted few-shot anchors for low-frequency items.
- Risk: PII handling disagreements.
  Mitigation: we’ll support both masked tokens and redaction; we will produce a small redaction-report as part of the deliverables.

Next steps: If Emma confirms the 2027-09-07 upload date I’ll schedule the bench run for 09-08 (auto suite) and book a short readout for 09-11.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Product Manager, Evaluation | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
